page: Microsoft Azure EC64ads_cc_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 512 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. Additionally, it includes 2458 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage configurations.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, scoring in the top 25% for multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests. Memory performance is particularly notable, with the PassMark memory score reaching the top 10% tier and cached memory bandwidth exceeding 4160 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also rank in the top 25%, processing 62.79 million operations per second. However, large-block uncached memory read and write speeds fall into the average range, and large-model LLM text generation shows weaker performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the EC64ads_cc_v5 offers high resource density by bundling substantial memory capacity and over 2.4 TB of local storage within a single instance, reducing the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput tasks. This hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale Redis deployments, data processing pipelines, and multi-threaded decompression workloads.
description: The Microsoft Azure EC64ads_cc_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by a 3.525 GHz AMD EPYC 7763 processor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs, 512 GB of RAM, and 2458 GB of bundled local storage. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers top-tier memory performance, with its PassMark memory score ranking in the top 10% and cached memory bandwidth reaching 4162.65 GB/sec. Multi-core processing and database operations, including Redis SET operations at 62.79 million operations per second, consistently place in the top 25% of benchmarks. While large-block uncached memory transfers and large-model LLM text generation represent performance tradeoffs, the server's high resource density makes it highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive databases, caching layers, and data-heavy enterprise workloads.
